//: npm, with package-lock.json committed -- and the lockfile is the whole
reason this works. Do not delete it.
Without it, `npm install` resolves the dependency tree from scratch, and
npm 10 crashes doing that on this project: 'Cannot read properties of
null (reading edgesOut)', thrown while working out vitest's peer
dependencies. It crashes before installing anything, so the build never
starts. That is an npm bug, not a bad dependency.
Vercel hid this for a while by caching node_modules between builds -- the
resolve was warm, so nothing crashed. The moment a build had to resolve
cold, every deployment failed, and a failed deployment on Vercel looks
exactly like a slow one: the site keeps serving the last good build.
The lockfile was generated with `npm install --legacy-peer-deps`, which
skips the peer resolution that crashes. Once it exists, plain
`npm install` reads it instead of resolving, and is fine. Regenerate it
the same way if it ever needs rebuilding.
It also fixes something worth keeping: builds now install the exact
versions recorded here, instead of whatever the registry offers that day.
